name: Level_2 - Task_2
description:
Study the glass transition of sodium silicate during cooling and reheating, and assess how the thermal history affects the inferred transition temperature. Start from the supplied molten structure at 4000 K. Use the supplied BKS-type Buckingham-Coulomb potential with PPPM electrostatics in LAMMPS, real units, charge atom style, periodic boundaries, and isotropic NPT dynamics at zero target pressure throughout.

Cool continuously from 4000 K to 300 K at 10 K/ps, hold at 300 K for 100 ps, then reheat continuously to 2600 K at 10 K/ps. Carry the same system through all stages without replacing atoms or reinitializing velocities. Choose and document suitable integration, thermostat, barostat, and sampling settings. Record elapsed time, target and measured temperature, pressure, and density at sufficient resolution to examine each stage and reproduce the analysis.

Estimate the cooling and reheating glass-transition temperatures from the density response using measured temperature as the temperature coordinate. Choose and document your estimator and the data it uses. Report both transition estimates and their signed difference, reheating minus cooling, in kelvin. For the 300 K hold, report representative mean temperature and density and quantify density drift using justified analysis windows. Assess the evidence for equilibration and explain any limitations of interpreting the observed transition or hold behavior.

Submit a JSON manifest linking the numerical results, structured JSON analysis and validation data, scripts, settings, LAMMPS inputs, raw logs, and thermal traces. Include restartable states at stage boundaries that preserve the cell, atom identities, positions, charges, and velocities, with timing information sufficient to assess continuity. Provide the data selections and estimator details needed to reproduce the reported estimates.
submission_format:
Fill in the blank manifest below and submit its path inside the task workspace
(for example, output/manifest.json). Linked paths may be relative to the manifest.
Replace null, empty strings and arrays with your results, file paths and data;
repeat example records and replace <...> keys with your actual identifiers.
Fixed units and method names describe the illustrated format. Where the task
leaves a method open, choose and record your method. Retain raw evidence and
calculations for any alternative method; unsupported calculations require
independent review before a final score.
